newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah guerrillas kill Israeli soldier.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah guerrillas kill Israeli soldier.

text.p: An Israeli soldier was killed in fierce fighting with pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas in south Lebanon on Sunday, Israeli-backed militia sources said.

In retaliation, Israeli warplanes launched three separate raids on Hizbollah positions in the area. Israeli artillery also engaged the guerrillas in duels in which two Lebanese civilians, including a seven-year-old boy, were wounded.
The soldier was wounded in Sojoud area on the edge of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone and later died of his wounds. There was no word from Israel on the soldier's death.
In Beirut, a Hizbollah spokesman claimed responsibility for the Sojoud attack and said several Israeli soldiers were killed.
"The Islamic resistance attacked an Israeli unit in Sojoud and several Zionist soldiers were killed and several were wounded," he said.
"Israeli helicopters tried to rescue the injured but they failed. There is heavy fighting and the Israeli helicopters have carried out many raids on Sojoud," the spokesman added.

Shortly after the attack, Israeli planes fired a total of 10 rockets at two different sectors of Iqlim al-Toufah mountain ridge which is used by Hizbollah guerrillas as a launching pad for attacks on the occupation zone, witnesses said.
There was no immediate word on casualties in the three raids.
In Jerusalem an army spokesman confirmed the raids and said "the targets that were hit were used as firing positions of the terrorists. The pilots reported accurate hits on the targets".
Hizbollah guerrillas are fighting to oust Israeli troops and their local militia allies from the 15-km (nine miles)-wide border zone they hold in south Lebanon.

Israel has held the border strip uninterruptedly since its first invasion of Lebanon in 1978. It set the current boundaries of the zone in 1985 after withdrawing the bulk of its forces following a second invasion in 1982.
